verses.text: David complains to God of his enemies, ver.
Comforts himself in God, and the experience of his goodness, ver.
Triumphs in the salvation of God, ver.
7, 8 A psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.
My soul - Of me: the soul being commonly put for the person.
In God - God hath utterly forsaken him.
Selah - This word is no where used but in this poetical book, and in the song of Habakkuk.
Probably it was a musical note, directing the singer either to lift up his voice, to make a pause, or to lengthen the tune.
But withal, it is generally placed at some remarkable passage; which gives occasion to think that it served also to quicken the attention of the singer and hearer.
My glory - Thou hast formerly given, and wilt farther give occasion of glorying in thy power and favour.
Lifter up - Thou wilt restore me to my former power and dignity.
His hill - Out of heaven, so called, chap. xv, 1.
Slept - Securely, casting all my cares upon God.
Awaked - After a sweet and undisturbed sleep.
Cheek bone - Which implies contempt and reproach.
Teeth - Their strength and the instruments of their cruelty.
He compares them to wild beasts.
